title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, retrospectives and roadmap Q4 2026
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:
This document is the canonical platform engineering reference for systems and services ownership, runbooks, dashboards & alerts, a short retrospective of Q3 incidents, and the roadmap for Q4 2026. It is intended for on-call engineers, platform owners, and engineering managers who operate or integrate with Redwood's platform services.

Summary / intent:
- Consolidate operational runbooks and dashboard references in one place.
- Provide reproducible how-tos for common maintenance tasks (dashboards, alerts, runbook updates).
- Record recent retrospectives and remediation action items.
- Align on Q4 roadmap and owners for platform reliability improvements.

1) Systems & Services inventory (top-level)
The table below lists the primary platform services, their primary owner, SLO, key dashboards and runbook pointer. If you modify or onboard a service, follow the "Runbook onboarding" procedure (section 3).

| service | primary_owner | SLO (p99 latency / availability) | key_dashboard | runbook |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| platform-api | eng-platform (team) | p99 < 200ms; 99.95% availability | Platform / API Overview (dash-id: PLAT-API-01) | /runbooks/platform-api |
| metrics-pipeline | eng-observability | end-to-end latency < 5m; 99.9% throughput | Metrics / Ingest (dash-id: MET-INGEST-02) | /runbooks/metrics-pipeline |
| auth-proxy | eng-security | auth latency p99 < 100ms; 99.99% availability | Security / Auth Proxy (dash-id: AUTH-01) | /runbooks/auth-proxy |
| kv-cache | eng-serving-runtime | cache hit-rate > 85%; p99 serve < 50ms | Serving / KV Cache (dash-id: KV-01) | /runbooks/kv-cache |
| orchestration | eng-platform | job success rate > 99.5%; median schedule < 30s | Orchestration / Jobs (dash-id: ORCH-01) | /runbooks/orchestration |

2) Dashboards and alerts (how we monitor)
Key dashboards (owner, purpose, primary panels):
- Platform / API Overview (PLAT-API-01) — request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate by route, tail-latency heatmap, token throughput and GPU utilization. Owner: eng-platform.
- Metrics / Ingest (MET-INGEST-02) — Kafka lag, partition throughput, consumer group health, E2E processing latency. Owner: eng-observability.
- Serving / KV Cache (KV-01) — cache hit ratio, eviction rate, mem usage, effect on downstream p99 latency. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Alerting conventions (named thresholds):
- Sev-1: Immediate page — availability < 99.9% (5m rolling), error rate > 5% (5m), or p99 latency > 2x SLO for > 10m. Pager duty: platform-prod.
- Sev-2: Page for high-impact degradations — throughput drop > 30% without scheduled maintenance, or queue depth > 10k for > 15m. Pager duty: platform-oncall.
- Sev-3: Ticket / Slack — moderate increase in errors or sustained latency increases that do not violate SLO for > 60m.

Alert detail examples:
- PLAT_API_5xx_ratio — triggers sev-1 if 5m error rate > 5% and > 1000 requests/min. Runbook: investigate 5xx by service_revision / route -> rollback or traffic-reroute.
- METRICS_INGEST_LAG — triggers sev-2 if consumer_lag > 200000 for > 10m. Runbook: check consumer group, broker health, and restart ingestion consumers if necessary.

3) Runbooks (procedures)
A. On-call checklist (immediate actions for any sev-1):
1. Acknowledge the page in PagerDuty and post an incident thread in #platform-incidents Slack channel.
2. Identify scope: which service(s), regions, customers affected. Update incident bridge.
3. Retrieve key dashboards (PLAT-API-01, KV-01, ORCH-01) and paste top 3 panels into the incident thread.
4. If a recent deploy is suspected, run: git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline origin/main and note the last deploy_tag; promote rollback if safe.
5. Execute mitigation (traffic shift to healthy region/model variant or enable fallback) and confirm recovery before declaring mitigation complete.
6. Declare postmortem owner within 24 hours.

B. Service-specific quick runbook: metrics-pipeline consumer lag (runbook excerpt)
1. Check consumer lag: kubectl -n observability exec -it svc/metrics-consumer -- curl localhost:9090/lag
2. If lag > 200k, check broker metrics (kafka-broker-1: 9092) and pod restarts: kubectl get pods -n observability --sort-by=.status.startTime
3. Restart consumer (graceful): kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-consumer -n observability.
4. If restarts fail or lag does not reduce after 10m, escalate to eng-observability and open a ticket.

C. Runbook maintenance (when to update)
- Ownership change, SLO changes, new alert thresholds, or after a postmortem action item.
- Procedure: submit a PR to the platform-runbooks repo, include test steps and update the dashboard panel links. Reviewer: runbooks@redwood.ai (eng-platform).

4) How-tos (common platform tasks)
How to add a panel to the PLAT-API-01 dashboard:
1. Open Grafana -> folder "Platform" -> PLAT-API-01.
2. Click "Edit" -> "Add panel" -> paste PromQL from the reference snippets below.
3. Use panel tags: component=platform-api, owner=eng-platform.
4. Save with versioned commit message: "dashboard(PLAT-API-01): add panel <name> — owner @<owner>".

How to create an alert policy (steps):
1. Draft PromQL and test in Explore.
2. Add panel to dashboard and create an alert rule in alerting UI.
3. Use naming convention: <SERVICE>_<METRIC>_<THRESHOLD> (e.g., PLATAPI_5xx_ratio_5p).
4. Set notification route: platform-prod -> pagerduty platform-prod (sev-1) or platform-oncall (sev-2).
5. Add runbook pointer URL and on-call rotation in the alert description.

5) Retrospective (Q3 2026) — incidents and remediation
Summary of top incidents in Q3:
- July 14: Platform API tail latency spike (root cause: new kernel scheduling change). Severity: sev-1. Customer impact: increased p99 from 180ms to 1.2s for 18min. Action: rolled back kernel change, added integration test for tail-latency under multi-tenant load. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- August 22: Metrics pipeline backlog due to consumer misconfiguration after a deployment. Severity: sev-2. Impact: delayed metrics and reduced observability for 2 hours. Action: consumer auto-restart and pre-deploy consumer-lag smoke test added. Owner: eng-observability.
- September 9: Cache eviction storm during scale event. Severity: sev-2. Impact: increased upstream cost and latency. Action: change cache warm-up policy, add proactive eviction monitoring. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.

Retrospective action items (status):
- A1: Add tail-latency CI job (Owner: eng-serving-runtime) — In progress, target complete 2026-11-30.
- A2: Consumer-lag smoke tests in CI (Owner: eng-observability) — Completed 2026-10-18.
- A3: Dashboard coverage audit for all services (Owner: eng-platform) — In progress, expected 2026-12-15.

6) Q4 2026 roadmap (prioritized)
- Reliability: tail-latency CI and synthetic multi-tenant load testing (eng-serving-runtime) — Q4.
- Observability: unified alerts routing and dynamic escalation policies (eng-observability + eng-platform) — Q4.
- Efficiency: intelligent batching tuning dashboard and recommendations in Redwood Optimize (eng-platform + eng-serving-runtime) — Q4.
- Runbook improvements: convert top 10 runbooks to checklist-driven playbooks with embedded runbook-run (eng-platform) — Q4.
- Onboarding: service onboarding checklist & automated runbook template generator (runbook PR pipeline) — Q4.

Owners and success criteria (short):
- eng-serving-runtime: pass tail-latency job for 3 consecutive weekly runs; reduce sev-1 tail incidents by 80% vs. Q3.
- eng-observability: migrate 90% of Sev-1 alerts to new routing rules and reduce noise by 40%.
- eng-platform: complete runbook audit and onboard 8 services to checklist format.

7) Team wiki & knowledge base pointers
- Platform team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q1
- Playbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-playbook-2026-q3
- Incident postmortems canonical folder: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems

Contact & escalation (on-call rotations)
- Primary PagerDuty: platform-prod (sev-1) — engineering operations SRE rotation.
- Secondary PagerDuty: platform-oncall (sev-2) — platform engineers.
- Escalation emails: oncall-escalate@redwood.ai (for after-hours exec notifications).

Appendix: small config snippets and references
- PromQL example (p99 latency): 
  quantile_over_time(0.99, request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"platform-api\"}[5m])

- Example alert JSON (short form):
  { \"alert\": \"PLAT_API_5xx_ratio_5p\", \"expr\": \"sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\\\"platform-api\\\",status=~\\\"5..\\\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\\\"platform-api\\\"}[5m])) > 0.05\" }

- Runbook PR template (summary): title, service, owner, SLOs updated, alert rules modified, test steps, rollback plan.

Notes / governance:
- This document is reviewed quarterly and after every sev-1 incident. For changes to SLOs or confidentiality-sensitive content consult eng-sre and security-and-compliance.

If you are onboarding a new service or need clarification, ping eng-platform in Slack or open an RFC in the platform repo.
